text:
Intention is the leader of things;
intention is first, they’re made by intention.
If with corrupt intent
you speak or act,
suffering follows you,
like a wheel, the ox’s foot.
Intention is the leader of things;
intention is first, they’re made by intention.
If with pure intent
you speak or act,
happiness follows you
like a shadow that never leaves.
note: Choices and consequences; how intentions shape our lives

text:
“They abused me, they hit me!
They beat me, they robbed me!”
For those who bear such a grudge,
hatred is never laid to rest.
“They abused me, they hit me!
They beat me, they robbed me!”
For those who bear no such grudge,
hatred is laid to rest.
note: Holding a grudge after being wronged

text:
For never is hatred
laid to rest by hate,
it’s laid to rest by love:
this is an ancient teaching.
note: Anger, conflict, wanting revenge

text:
By hard work and diligence,
by restraint and by self-control,
a smart person would build an island
that the floods cannot overflow.
note: Building inner stability amid overwhelming circumstances

text:
The mind quivers and quakes,
hard to guard, hard to curb.
The discerning straighten it out,
like a fletcher an arrow.
note: Anxious, restless mind; regaining focus
Scattered thoughts; learning to settle the mind

text:
All too soon this body
will lie upon the earth,
bereft of consciousness,
tossed aside like a worthless log.
note: Mortality, ageing, facing death

text:
A wrongly directed mind
would do you more harm
than a hater to the hated,
or an enemy to their foe.
note: Self-sabotage; harmful thought patterns

text:
Don’t find fault with others,
with what they’ve done or left undone.
You should only watch yourself,
what you’ve done or left undone.
note: Judging others; resentment about others' behaviour

text:
From a heap of trash
discarded on the highway,
a lotus might blossom,
fragrant and delightful.
note: Hope from hard beginnings; feeling worthless

text:
If while wandering you find no partner
equal or better than yourself,
then firmly resolve to wander alone—
there’s no fellowship with fools.
note: Loneliness; choosing solitude over bad company

text:
The fool who thinks they’re a fool
is wise at least to that extent.
But the true fool is said to be one
who imagines that they are wise.
note: Feeling foolish; humility and self-awareness

text:
It’s not good to do a deed
that plagues you later on,
for which you weep and wail,
as its effect stays with you.
It is good to do a deed
that doesn’t plague you later on,
that gladdens and cheers,
as its effect stays with you.
note: Regret, guilt, weighing a decision

text:
Regard one who sees your faults
as a guide to a hidden treasure.
Stay close to one so intelligent and astute
who curbs you when you need it.
Sticking close to such an impartial person,
things get better, not worse.
note: Receiving criticism; valuing honest friends

text:
As the wind cannot stir
a solid mass of rock,
so too blame and praise
do not affect the wise.
note: Hurt by criticism or craving approval

text:
True persons give up everything,
they don’t cajole for the things they desire.
Though touched by sadness or happiness,
the astute appear neither depressed nor elated.
note: Emotional ups and downs; equanimity
Ambition and temptation to cut ethical corners

text:
Better than a thousand
meaningless sayings
is a single meaningful saying,
hearing which brings you peace.
note: Information overload; seeking what truly matters

text:
The supreme conqueror is
not he who conquers a million men in battle,
but he who conquers a single man:
himself.
note: Self-mastery; struggling with one's own impulses

text:
Better to live a single day
energetic and strong,
than to live a hundred years
lazy and lacking energy.
note: Lethargy; quality of a life over its length

text:
If you do something bad,
don’t do it again and again,
don’t set your heart on it,
for piling up evil is suffering.
note: Guilt after a mistake; not repeating it

text:
Think not lightly of evil,
that it won’t come back to you.
The pot is filled with water
falling drop by drop;
the fool is filled with wickedness
piled up bit by bit.
note: Small bad habits adding up over time

text:
Don’t speak harshly,
they may speak harshly back.
For aggressive speech is painful,
and the rod may spring back on you.
note: Anger in conversation; harsh words returning

text:
If you still yourself
like a broken gong,
you reach extinguishment
and know no conflict.
note: Staying quiet amid conflict; inner stillness

text:
What is joy, what is laughter,
when the flames are ever burning?
Swathed in darkness,
would you not seek a light?
note: Feeling lost in darkness; seeking meaning

text:
Fancy chariots of kings wear out,
and even this body gets old.
But the truth of the good never gets old—
so the good proclaim to the good.
note: Ageing body; what endures

text:
A person of little learning
ages like an ox—
their flesh grows,
but not their wisdom.
note: Growing older without growing wiser

text:
When young they spurned the spiritual path
and failed to earn any wealth.
Now they lie like spent arrows,
bemoaning over things past.
note: Regret in later life over wasted youth

text:
If one were to treat oneself
as one instructs another,
the well-tamed indeed would tame:
for the self, it seems, is hard to tame.
note: Giving advice we don't follow ourselves

text:
One is indeed the lord of oneself,
for who else would be one’s lord?
By means of a well-tamed self,
one gains a lord that’s rare indeed.
note: Self-reliance; taking charge of oneself

text:
It’s easy to do bad things
harmful to oneself,
but good things that are helpful
are the hardest things to do.
note: Struggling to do the hard, right thing

text:
For it is by oneself that evil’s done,
one is corrupted by oneself.
It’s by oneself that evil’s not done,
one is purified by oneself.
Purity and impurity are personal matters,
no one can purify another.
note: Personal responsibility; no one can change you

text:
Never neglect what is good for yourself
for the sake of another, however great.
Knowing well what is good for yourself,
be intent upon your heart’s goal.
note: Losing yourself serving others; keeping your purpose

text:
Get up, don’t be heedless,
live by principle, with good conduct.
For one of good conduct sleeps at ease,
in this world and the next.
note: Clear conscience; living well to rest easy

text:
Someone whose bad deed
is supplanted by the good,
shines upon this world,
like the moon freed from clouds.
note: Redemption after wrongdoing; starting over

text:
Even if it were raining money,
you’d not be sated in sensual pleasures.
An astute person understands that sensual pleasures
offer little gratification and much suffering.
note: Wanting more; pleasure and money never satisfy

text:
Let us live so very happily,
loving among the hostile.
Among hostile humans,
let us live with love.
note: Staying kind among hostile people

text:
Victory breeds enmity;
the defeated sleep badly.
The peaceful sleep at ease,
having left victory and defeat behind.
note: Competition, winning and losing; finding peace
Contentment; what truly matters

text:
Don’t ever get too close
to those you like or dislike.
For not seeing the liked is suffering,
and so is seeing the disliked.
note: Attachment and aversion in relationships

text:
Sorrow springs from what we hold dear,
fear springs from what we hold dear;
one free from holding anything dear
has no sorrow, let alone fear.
note: Grief and fear of losing loved things

text:
Sorrow springs from desire,
fear springs from desire;
one free from desire
has no sorrow, let alone fear.
note: Fear and sorrow rooted in wanting

text:
When anger surges like a lurching chariot,
keep it in check.
That’s what I call a charioteer;
others just hold the reins.
note: Holding back anger in the moment

text:
Defeat anger with kindness,
villainy with virtue,
stinginess with giving,
and lies with truth.
note: Responding to wrongs with their opposite

text:
It’s always been this way, Atula,
it’s not just today.
They blame you when you’re silent,
they blame you when you speak a lot,
and even when you speak just right:
no one in the world escapes blame.
There never was, nor will be,
nor is there today,
someone who is wholly praised
or wholly blamed.
note: Being criticised no matter what you do

text:
A smart person would purge
their own stains gradually,
bit by bit, moment by moment,
like a smith smelting silver.
note: Changing your faults slowly and patiently

text:
Life is easy for the shameless.
With all the rude courage of a crow,
they live pushy,
rude, and corrupt.
Life is hard for the conscientious,
always seeking purity,
neither clinging nor rude,
pure of livelihood and discerning.
note: Integrity feels harder than cutting corners

text:
There is no fire like greed,
no crime like hate,
no net like delusion,
no river like craving.
note: Greed, hate and craving as traps

text:
It’s easy to see the faults of others,
hard to see one’s own.
For the faults of others
are tossed high like hay,
while one’s own are hidden,
as a cheat hides a bad hand.
note: Judging others while missing your own faults

text:
When you look for the flaws of others,
always finding fault,
your defilements only grow,
you’re far from ending defilements.
note: Constant fault-finding harms the critic

text:
You don’t become just
by passing hasty judgment.
An astute person evaluates both
what is pertinent and what is irrelevant.
note: Slowing down before judging

text:
You’re not an astute scholar
just because you speak a lot.
One who is secure, free of enmity and fear,
is said to be astute.
note: Real wisdom versus talking a lot
Ageing without growing wiser

text:
You yourselves must do the work,
the Realized Ones just show the way.
note: No one can do your inner work

text:
All conditions are impermanent—
when this is seen with wisdom,
one grows disillusioned with suffering:
this is the path to purity.
note: Accepting that everything changes

text:
They don’t get going when it’s time to start;
they’re young and strong, but given to sloth.
Their mind depressed in sunken thought,
lazy and slothful, they can’t discern the path.
note: Procrastination and wasted youthful energy

text:
From meditation springs wisdom,
without meditation, wisdom ends.
Knowing these two paths—
of progress and decline—
you should conduct yourself
so that wisdom grows.
note: Practice as the source of wisdom

text:
If by giving up material happiness
one sees abundant happiness,
the attentive would give up material happiness,
seeing the abundant happiness.
note: Trading small pleasures for deeper contentment

text:
Seeking their own happiness
by imposing suffering on others,
intimate with enmity,
they’re not freed from enmity.
note: Happiness at others' expense backfires

text:
The good shine from afar,
like the Himalayan peaks,
but the wicked are not seen,
like arrows scattered in the night.
note: Goodness is noticed over time

text:
Sitting alone, sleeping alone,
tirelessly wandering alone;
one who tames themselves alone
would delight within a forest.
note: Finding contentment in solitude

text:
A bad deed is better left undone,
for it will plague you later on.
A good deed is better done,
one that does not plague you.
note: Choices that leave guilt or peace

text:
Like an elephant struck
with arrows in battle,
I shall endure abuse,
for so many folk are badly behaved.
note: Bearing insults and mistreatment calmly

text:
In the past my mind wandered
how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased.
Now I’ll carefully guide it,
as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.
note: Restless, scattered mind; resolving to take charge of it

text:
Delight in diligence!
Take good care of your mind!
Pull yourself out of this pit,
like an elephant sunk in a bog.
note: Feeling stuck; finding effort to climb out

text:
If you find an alert companion,
an attentive friend to live happily together,
then, overcoming all adversities,
wander with them, joyful and mindful.

If you find no alert companion,
no attentive friend to live happily together,
then, like a king who flees his conquered realm,
wander alone like a tusker in the wilds.
note: Friendship, loneliness, choosing good company or solitude
Gratitude and contentment with what you have

text:
Whoever is beaten by this wretched craving,
this attachment to the world,
their sorrow grows,
like grass in the rain.

But whoever prevails over this wretched craving,
so hard to get over in the world,
their sorrows fall from them,
like a drop from a lotus-leaf.
note: Wanting too much; how letting go eases sorrow

text:
A tree grows back even when cut down,
so long as its roots are strong and undamaged;
suffering springs up again and again,
so long as the tendency to craving is not pulled out.
note: Same pain keeps returning; addressing root causes

text:
Let go of the past, let go of the future,
let go of the present, having gone beyond rebirth.
With your heart freed in every respect,
you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
note: Regret and worry; letting go of past and future

text:
Riches ruin a simpleton,
but not a seeker of the far shore.
From craving for wealth, a simpleton
ruins themselves and others.
note: Greed for money harming oneself and others

text:
Mix with spiritual friends,
who are tireless and pure of livelihood.
Share what you have with others,
being skillful in your conduct.
And when you’re full of joy,
you’ll make an end to suffering.
note: Good company, generosity and joy

text:
Urge yourself on,
reflect on yourself.
A mendicant self-controlled and mindful
will always dwell in happiness.

Self is indeed the lord of self,
for who else would be one’s lord?
Self is indeed the home of self,
so restrain yourself,
as a merchant his thoroughbred steed.
note: Self-reliance and self-discipline; taking responsibility for yourself

text:
Nothing is better for a brahmin
than to hold their mind back from attachment.
From wherever a cruel wish recoils,
right there suffering subsides.
note: Wanting to hurt someone; restraint eases suffering

text:
Why the matted hair, you simpleton,
and why the skin of deer?
The tangle is inside you,
yet you polish up your outsides.
note: Fixing appearances while ignoring inner turmoil

text:
Abuse, killing, caging:
they endure these without anger.
Patience is their powerful army:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
note: Mistreated by others; patience instead of anger

text:
Not fighting among those who fight,
quenched among those who have taken up arms,
not grasping among those who grasp:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
note: Staying calm amid conflict and competition

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: Once the ideal is chosen and the means determined, we may almost let go the ideal, because we are sure it will be there, when the means are perfected. When the cause is there, there is no more difficulty about the effect, the effect is bound to come. If we take care of the cause, the effect will take care of itself.
note: Anxious about results; focus on the work itself

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: If we examine our own lives, we find that the greatest cause of sorrow is this: we take up something, and put our whole energy on it — perhaps it is a failure and yet we cannot give it up. We know that it is hurting us, that any further clinging to it is simply bringing misery on us; still, we cannot tear ourselves away from it. The bee came to sip the honey, but its feet stuck to the honey-pot and it could not get away.
note: Unable to let go of something that is hurting you

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: That is the one cause of misery: we are attached, we are being caught. Therefore says the Gita: Work constantly; work, but be not attached; be not caught. Reserve unto yourself the power of detaching yourself from everything, however beloved, however much the soul might yearn for it, however great the pangs of misery you feel if you were going to leave it; still, reserve the power of leaving it whenever you want.
note: Committing fully while keeping the freedom to let go

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: There are men who are never attracted by anything. They can never love, they are hard-hearted and apathetic; they escape most of the miseries of life. But the wall never feels misery, the wall never loves, is never hurt; but it is the wall, after all. Surely it is better to be attached and caught, than to be a wall.
note: Tempted to close your heart to avoid getting hurt

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: We get caught. How? Not by what we give, but by what we expect. We get misery in return for our love; not from the fact that we love, but from the fact that we want love in return. There is no misery where there is no want.
note: Hurt by unreturned love or unmet expectations

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: Ask nothing; want nothing in return. Give what you have to give; it will come back to you — but do not think of that now, it will come back multiplied a thousandfold — but the attention must not be on that. Yet have the power to give: give, and there it ends.
note: Giving without keeping score

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: Every day we renew our determination to be unattached. We cast our eyes back and look at the past objects of our love and attachment, and feel how every one of them made us miserable. We went down into the depths of despondency because of our “love”! We found ourselves mere slaves in the hands of others, we were dragged down and down! And we make a fresh determination: “Henceforth, I will be master of myself; henceforth, I will have control over myself.” But the time comes, and the same story once more! Again the soul is caught and cannot get out. The bird is in a net, struggling and fluttering.
note: Falling back into the same painful patterns

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: I know the difficulties. Tremendous they are, and ninety per cent of us become discouraged and lose heart, and in our turn, often become pessimists and cease to believe in sincerity, love, and all that is grand and noble. So, we find men who in the freshness of their lives have been forgiving, kind, simple, and guileless, become in old age lying masks of men.
note: Discouragement hardening into cynicism over the years

display: Lectures (Complete Works, Vol. II): Work And Its Secret
text: We are all the time, from our childhood, trying to lay the blame upon something outside ourselves. We are always standing up to set right other people, and not ourselves. If we are miserable, we say, “Oh, the world is a devil’s world.” We curse others and say, “What infatuated fools!” But why should we be in such a world, if we really are so good?
note: Blaming others and the world for our unhappiness
